copyright: Colourful homes line Nyhavn Canal, Copenhagen, Denmark (© emicristea/Getty Images)
description: In Copenhagen, Nyhavn Canal is a burst of colour and history. Lined with bright, gabled townhouses reflected in the water, this 17th-century waterfront is one of Denmark's best-known landmarks.

copyright: Joshua Tree National Park, California, United States (© JJ Landscapes/Getty Images)
description: Where two great deserts meet, Joshua Tree National Park reveals a stark, mesmerising landscape shaped by wind, time and extremes. In Southern California, United States, the higher Mojave Desert merges with the hotter, lower Colorado Desert, creating a unique blend of ecosystems and remarkable biodiversity.

copyright: Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre, New Caledonia (© Fabien Astre/Alamy)
copyrightKeyword: International Day of the Worlds Indigenous Peoples
description: Today, the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples invites a closer look at communities whose stories stretch far beyond recorded history. Proclaimed by the United Nations in 1994 and first observed in 1995, the day commemorates a landmark 1982 meeting on Indigenous rights. More than 476 million Indigenous people live across about 90 countries, representing thousands of cultures and protecting an estimated 80% of the planet's remaining biodiversity despite making up around 6% of the global population.

copyright: Infinity Bridge in Stockton-on-Tees, England (© Bahadir Yeniceri/Shutterstock)
description: On 8 August, curiosity takes centre stage on International Infinity Day—a celebration inspired by the sideways figure 8, a symbol of something without end. Founded in 1987 by New York–based philosopher Jean-Pierre Ady Fenyo, the date (8/8) was chosen because the number 8, when turned on its side, becomes the infinity symbol, or lemniscate, first introduced by English mathematician John Wallis in 1655. The day celebrates philosophy, science, art and the endless possibilities of human imagination.

copyright: Hoodoos in Ah‑Shi‑Sle‑Pah Wilderness in San Juan County, New Mexico, United States (© Westend61/Getty Images)
description: Nature has a knack for balancing the impossible. In New Mexico's Ah-Shi-Sle-Pah Wilderness in the United States, towering hoodoos perch hefty rock caps on slender stems. Wind, water and ice have spent roughly 75 million years sculpting these remote badlands into an open-air gallery that feels more alien than terrestrial.

copyright: Migrating wildebeest crossing Mara River in Masai Mara, Kenya (© Manoj Shah/Getty Images)
description: In the Masai Mara, Kenya, the ground seems to move. A vast surge of wildebeest—hoofed grazers built for endurance—travel in tightly packed herds, drawn by fresh grass and water replenished by seasonal rains.

copyright: Decorated gate of the Royal Palace of Fez, Morocco (© cgst26/Shutterstock)
description: In Fez, Morocco, the Royal Palace—known as Dar al-Makhzen—has stood as a seat of power since the 13th century, when Morocco's rulers established a fortified royal city around it. Behind its high walls lie gardens, courtyards, mosques and royal residences spread across a vast complex still used by the king today, making it both historic and fully active.
